recentItems.title: How Gen Z sees the world: Young American discovers the real China
recentItems.description:
Kyle Sykes, a young American, came to China hoping to understand the country beyond what he had seen in the media and read online. After living and studying in the country, he was impressed by the convenience of everyday life, rapid technological and infrastructure development, and the warmth of the Chinese people.

From hiking the Great Wall and exploring the Forbidden City to experiencing the vibrant cities of Shenzhen and Shanghai, Kyle says these firsthand experiences gave him a deeper understanding of China's history, culture and modern development. He also experienced the warmth of Chinese friends at a burger festival in Beijing, where food and laughter brought young people from different cultures closer together.

Having personally benefited from China-US educational exchange, Kyle hopes young people from both countries can continue to strengthen communication, mutual understanding and friendship, and contribute to a more peaceful and prosperous future.

recentItems.title: What happens when TCM joins Western medicine in global healthcare?
recentItems.description:
How can we best optimize critical care and the fight against infectious diseases? Dr. Liu Qingquan, president of the Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Capital Medical University, shares how modern tech like ECMO can sustain life, while TCM restores organ function, aids machine weaning and combats antibiotic resistance. Facing threats like "Virus X," China's core strength lies in integrating TCM with Western medicine to safeguard global health.

recentItems.title: Expert: TCM's holistic and preventive philosophy offers insights for global health
recentItems.description:
The holistic and preventive philosophy of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) provides insights for global healthcare, said Tong Xiaolin, academician at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Tong explained that TCM has a holistic therapeutic perspective, which does not simply look at a single indicator; rather, it places it within the whole person for consideration. 

There is also the concept of "treating disease before it arises." For example, some metabolic disorders and multiple metabolic disorders will ultimately lead to vascular problems. Traditional Chinese doctors will intervene early by treating the luo, or collaterals, at an early stage, when diabetic fundus lesions and kidney lesions have not yet been detected.

"When it comes to TCM's therapeutic philosophy, these two aspects stand out as particularly valuable for the world to learn from," Tong said.

recentItems.title: China's vision for BRICS: What does "pioneers of the times" mean?
recentItems.description:
At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping called on BRICS countries to become "pioneers of the times," highlighting four areas: Innovation, security, culture and governance. With BRICS representing around half of the world's population and playing an increasingly significant role in global economic growth, what does China envision for the future of the grouping and the wider Global South? What are the economic and geopolitical implications, and what could BRICS' evolution mean for the world and for you?

recentItems.title: New routes, new tech reshapes China-ASEAN business
recentItems.description:
At CAEXPO, Singapore Business Federation Executive Director Soo Wei-Chieh discusses how Chinese technology could be integrated into Singapore businesses and why companies on both sides are increasingly seeking collaboration.

He says new links such as the Pinglu Canal may reduce friction in moving goods, but businesses must still weigh total costs, market potential and the opportunities created by the new route.

recentItems.description:

If he were young again, he would explore opportunities in food and agriculture, education and healthcare, using technology to serve the diverse needs of ASEAN markets.
